guidance: Use the loose bulk density of the material as it sits in the trough, not its tapped or particle density, and take the trough loading from its flow class: 15% for abrasive, sluggish or lumpy material, 30% for an average powder, 45% for free-flowing non-abrasive granules. The selection tables the industry uses assume a standard pipe and a control-fed inlet; a screw flood loaded under a hopper needs its own design.
method: A screw conveyor is a volumetric machine: each turn carries the material that fills the annular flight area over one pitch. The CEMA form is Q = 0.7854 · (Ds² − Dp²) · P · K · 60 / 1728 cubic feet per hour per revolution, where Ds is the outside flight diameter, Dp the centre pipe diameter and P the pitch, all in inches, and K the trough loading as a fraction (0.45 for 45%). The same quantity in SI terms is Q = π/4 · (D² − d²) · P · n · 60 · K, with D, d and P in metres and n in revolutions per minute; 0.7854 is π/4 and 1,728 converts cubic inches to cubic feet. Mass capacity is the volumetric capacity times the loose bulk density. This page converts both unit systems to SI, computes the full flight area π/4 (D² − d²), the filled area and the volume per turn (area times pitch), multiplies by the speed and the loading, and reports m³/h and t/h with the US customary equivalent in ft³/h and short tons per hour (2,000 lb). It also reports the flight tip speed π D n / 60, which matters because abrasive wear rises quickly and a dust cloud is easier to ignite above about 1 m/s. Worked default: a 300 mm screw on a 76 mm pipe with a standard 300 mm pitch, 60 rpm, 30% loading and 800 kg/m³ gives a flight area of 661.49 cm², 19.84 litres per turn, 21.43 m³/h and 17.15 t/h, with a tip speed of 0.94 m/s. Against the published selection table a 12 in screw on a 3½ in pipe at a standard 12 in pitch and 30% loading carries 12.93 ft³/h per rpm, which is the table's 12.9. Inputs are limited to a screw diameter of 50 to 1,500 mm (2 to 60 in), a shaft of 0 to 1,200 mm (0 to 48 in) that must stay smaller than the screw, a pitch of 25 to 2,000 mm (1 to 80 in), a speed of 0 to 500 rpm, a trough loading of 5 to 45% and a bulk density of 50 to 4,000 kg/m³ (3 to 250 lb/ft³); a shaft as large as the screw is refused because the flight area would vanish, and a loading above 45% is refused because it is outside the range the capacity tables are built on. The page assumes a level trough, a standard full flight of constant pitch, a control-fed inlet, a loose bulk density that does not change along the conveyor, and material that does not arch, smear or pack; it does not apply the inclination correction (about 0.90 at 5°, 0.80 at 10°, 0.70 at 15° and 0.65 at 20°), the factors for cut, ribbon or paddle flights, the reduction for lump size, or the drive power, hanger bearing and shaft checks that a real selection needs.
